title: AI Factory onion architecture
summary: A lifecycle request travels from the outside in, and each layer calls only the layer inside it. Only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes Azure.

evidence.M1: Measured 2026-10-24: aif-ops and aif-event-relay runs of the lifecycle Function in jostrm/azure-enterprise-scale-byor-121 take 12-30 s each; scenario 1 for aif-126 went from the first prepare (13:22 UTC) to the repository-initialization commit (13:26 UTC) in 4 min.
evidence.M2: Measured from commit times in the jostrm/azure-enterprise-scale-byor-12x factory repositories, from 'Initialize reviewed AI Factory source pin' to 'Configure generated deployment connection': aif-124 103 min (2026-10-23), aif-125 131 min (2026-10-24), aif-123 236 min (2026-10-22, the day the Lifecycle-Function contract records an ARM 403 stop and a recovery).
evidence.M3: Measured 2026-10-24, aif-125 (aif-lifecycle-phase4-5-log.md): Function intake about 1 min, repository-initialization about 1 min, a 26 min gap before minimum-foundation, minimum-foundation to publication 02:33-04:25 CEST (network-foundation with VPN gateway done 04:12, runner 04:17), each COMMON review (prepare-next) about 12 min, COMMON start to GitHub run 17-19 min.
evidence.M4: Measured 2026-10-24: factory-lifecycle COMMON runs 40064071277 (4.0 min) and 40075915367 (3.3 min) in jostrm/azure-enterprise-scale-byor-125; both stopped before any Azure write, so COMMON and PROJECT deployment times are not measured yet.
evidence.M5: Measured 2026-10-22 on the real Factory API (Lifecycle-Function contract): a runtime review took 13 min and its confirmation held the catalog lock for 18 min.
evidence.M6: Measured 2026-10-24: one fix iteration, composite of pink v0.47.38 and v0.47.39 (aif-125).
evidence.E: Estimated from the code path and earlier factories; replace with measured values after real runs. Scenarios 4-6 ran simulated only (AIF_DELETES=simulate): the Factory API never saw a delete.

layers.label: L1
layers.name: Clients
layers.where: azurefactory CLI and Python SDK AzureFactoryClient (purple environment_setup/azurefactory-cli) · Tkinter wizard (pink) · MAUI ESAIF.ConfigWizard (jostrm/maui-apps)
layers.what: Thin clients: they build requests, show reviews, confirm and poll. No deployment logic lives here.
layers.called_by: The external consumer, or a person at the CLI or a wizard.
layers.calls: L2 over HTTP on loopback (127.0.0.1:8765) with the API key in X-API-Key; plaintext HTTP is allowed only on loopback.

change.note: SDK/CLI: stdlib-only, edit + tests + push, 15-25 min. MAUI: Windows build and installer, 30-60 min. The Tkinter wizard ships with the pink release (see L2).

layers.label: L2
layers.name: Factory REST API
layers.where: jostrm/azure-aifactory-config: FastAPI routes src/*_api.py and the service layer in src/ · runs as SYSTEM on 127.0.0.1:8765 on the admin VM
layers.what: Owns every decision: catalog, reviews, whole-workflow consent, recoveries and reconciliation, frozen deployment planner, cost preview, DPAPI-sealed SQLite state.
layers.called_by: L1 clients on the same host (catalog and deployment routes accept loopback clients only).
layers.calls: L3: runs purple Bash/PowerShell launchers and helpers, and dispatches the factory-lifecycle pipeline. Pins a purple commit.

change.note: One fix iteration now: run, diagnose, fix, tests, release, install, recovery, fresh review (see Code change - options). Estimated 70 min with the future options.

layers.label: L3
layers.name: Pipelines + API-called scripts
layers.where: purple bootstrap/ (launchers, lib/ helpers) and bootstrap/templates/factory-lifecycle-*.yml · pink vendors byte-exact copies in template-files/creation-workflow/bootstrap/lib
layers.what: What the API starts: Bash and PowerShell launchers on the API host, and GitHub Actions or ADO pipelines on the factory's self-hosted runner.
layers.called_by: L2. Pink's publication stage first commits the generated catalog, enrollment and settings to the consumer repository.
layers.calls: L4: the pipeline worker bootstrap/lib/factory_lifecycle.py compiles and deploys purple Bicep. Bootstrap helpers call ARM directly (L5).

layers.label: L5
layers.name: Azure Resource Manager
layers.where: management.azure.com: deployments, resource groups, resources, role assignments, locks
layers.what: The only layer that changes Azure. Most wall-clock time is spent here: networks, VPN gateway, private endpoints and DNS zones.
layers.example: group and subscription deployments · resource-group deletes · provider registration
layers.called_by: L4 deployments from the runner; L3 bootstrap helpers from the API host (az, with the VM's managed identity).
layers.calls: Nothing in AI Factory: Azure resource providers.

change.note: No AI Factory code. Platform conditions (quota, policy, provider registration, RBAC propagation) are fixed by configuration or with Azure support; the code change then lands in L4 (Bicep) or L2 (a pre-check).

prevention.fifth_bug: 2026-10-24 ~10:00, COMMON attempt 2 (run 40075915367): the worker refused with runtime-network-preservation-source-changed before any Azure write. The admin VM's Git for Windows has core.autocrlf=true (system), so the purple submodule and every catalog-run copy hold 12-networkCommon.bicep with CRLF (11,057 bytes, 255 CR) while git stores it LF (10,802 bytes, 0 CR) and the Linux runner checks out LF. The network-preservation proof hashes raw bytes, and its CRLF digest is frozen in the verified network-foundation profile.

steps.title: Five layers, one direction.
steps.explanation: A lifecycle request travels from the outside in. Each layer calls only the layer inside it, and only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes Azure. The outer layers are thin and quick to change; the inner layers do the slow work.
steps.key: Outer layers are fast to change. Inner layers are slow to run.

steps.title: An Azure Function enters through the SDK.
steps.explanation: The lifecycle Function offers the six scenarios as reviewed REST operations. It never calls the Factory API over the network: it dispatches aif-ops.yml to a management runner, which calls AzureFactoryClient next to the API.

steps.title: CLI, SDK and wizards are thin clients.
steps.explanation: The azurefactory CLI and Python SDK (purple), the Tkinter wizard (pink) and the MAUI ESAIF.ConfigWizard send the same review, confirm and status calls. They hold no deployment logic, so they spend seconds, not minutes.
steps.key: Clients review, confirm and poll. Deciding happens in layer 2.

steps.title: Pink owns the decisions.
steps.explanation: The FastAPI routes and the service layer behind them build the catalog, reviews, whole-workflow consent, frozen deployment plans, cost previews and recoveries. State is DPAPI-sealed SQLite on the admin VM, where the identity, VPN and runner are.
steps.key: A runtime review took 13 min and its confirmation 18 min (measured).

steps.title: The API starts scripts and pipelines.
steps.explanation: The API runs purple Bash and PowerShell such as GHA-update-aifactory-and-run-project.sh, create-new-aifactory-scaleset.sh and runner-registration.ps1, and dispatches factory-lifecycle.yml or the ADO pipeline on the factory's self-hosted runner.
steps.key: A COMMON run reached the worker after 3-4 min (measured, aif-125).

steps.title: Purple describes the infrastructure.
steps.explanation: The worker compiles and deploys purple Bicep: 11-rgCommon, 12-networkCommon and 13-rgLevel for COMMON, 31-network to 11-integration for a project. The pipelines also run scripts such as preflight.sh, subnetCalc_v2.ps1 and delete-services-if-disabled.sh.
steps.key: Build, preflight and what-if take minutes, not hours (estimated).

steps.title: Only the core changes Azure.
steps.explanation: ARM creates, updates and deletes resource groups and resources. Networking dominates: a VPN gateway alone takes tens of minutes, and private endpoints and private DNS zones add more.
steps.key: Most wall-clock time is spent in the core.

steps.title: Bootstrap skips layer 4.
steps.explanation: Scenario 1's bootstrap stages, repository-initialization to publication, run on the API host: pink plus vendored purple helpers call az, gh and git straight to ARM. Only COMMON, PROJECT and later operations go through the pipelines and Bicep.
steps.key: Bootstrap took 103-131 min on two factories (measured, aif-124 and aif-125).

steps.title: Six scenarios, one path.
steps.key: Inner layers cost the most time to change: prevent their bugs instead of looping faster.
